I am a fourth-year Computer Science major at the Indian Institute of Science Education and
Research Bhopal. I work on the problem of making entanglement reliable enough to build real
quantum networks, and on the broader question of how mathematical structure should guide
algorithm design.

I am currently a Summer Research Intern at UMass Amherst with the Centre for Quantum
Networks, advised by Dr. Filip Rozpedek and Dr. Stefan Krastanov. There I implement quantum
convolutional codes, entanglement purification protocols, and quantum repeater simulations
under realistic hardware noise in [QuantumClifford.jl](https://github.com/QuantumSavory/QuantumClifford.jl)
and [QuantumSavory.jl](https://github.com/QuantumSavory/QuantumSavory.jl).

In parallel, I am a research intern with Prof. Dominique Orban's group at Polytechnique
Montréal ([JuliaSmoothOptimizers](https://jso.dev)), translating classical smooth and
non-smooth optimization problems into structured Julia formulations (JuMP, ADNLPModels) for
[OptimizationProblems.jl](https://github.com/JuliaSmoothOptimizers/OptimizationProblems.jl).

Earlier research includes:

- Quantum Fisher information bounds on CP-phase sensitivity in long-baseline neutrino
  experiments (T2K, NOvA) with Dr. Naga Deepthi at Mahindra University
- Hybrid quantum-inspired optimization for fidelity-constrained entanglement routing and
  memory scheduling, as a QWorld QIntern
